title: A staker wired to a BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook on which it is not the recipient reverts on EVERY _syncBudget path
description: `pull()` is `onlyOwnerOrRecipient` and additionally reverts `RecipientUnset` when `recipient == address(0)`. The staker calls it with `msg.sender == itself`, so stake, unstake, claim, depositFor, initiateMigration and pullAndRefresh all revert unconditionally — even when mintDebt is zero. In a cross-staker migration the target staker is BY CONSTRUCTION not yet the hook's recipient, so wiring its dispatcherHook before flipping `hook.setRecipient` bricks the migration at the first `depositFor`, leaving a partially-executed migration with the batch's ERC1155 already pulled into the migrator.
impact: Availability only — no value at risk. pull() is onlyOwnerOrRecipient and additionally reverts RecipientUnset when recipient == address(0). The staker calls it with msg.sender == itself, so stake, unstake, claim, depositFor, initiateMigration and pullAndRefresh ALL revert unconditionally — even when mintDebt is zero. emergencyWithdraw and userMigrate never call pull(), so principal always escapes.
attackPath: 1. In a cross-staker migration the TARGET staker is BY CONSTRUCTION not yet the hook's recipient.
2. The operator wires the target's dispatcherHook before flipping hook.setRecipient.
3. Every _syncBudget path on the target now reverts.
4. The migration bricks at the first depositFor, leaving a PARTIALLY-EXECUTED migration with the batch's ERC1155 already pulled into the migrator.
likelihood: medium if the wiring order is not documented — and it is not.
assumptions: A recipient-guarded hook is wired to the target before the recipient flip.
justification: Low. The impact is a total interaction DoS on the target staker, which is a Medium-shaped availability signal, but three facts hold it at Low: recovery is clean and owner-side (two independent un-brick routes), principal always escapes via emergencyWithdraw/userMigrate, and no value is at risk at any point. Recorded with an explicit `medium` ceiling — if the operator judges a half-executed migration with custody already moved to be an availability event rather than a config slip, Medium is defensible.
recommendation: Document the wiring ORDER as a mandatory runbook step (flip hook.setRecipient BEFORE setDispatcherHook on the target), and add an orchestrator test that wires a real recipient-guarded hook to the target.

disclosedAgainst.label: L-02 (open, src/NFTStakerDepletion.sol — un-try/catch'd dispatcherHook.pull() lets an unauthorized hook DoS interactions and initiateMigration)
disclosedAgainst.basis: SANITIZER-ADDED DISCLOSURE per D-15. Same 'hook bricks every _syncBudget path' class recurring on copy #4 via a DIFFERENT trigger (recipient authorisation on pull(), vs a reverting/unauthorized hook). Disclosed, NOT collapsed, NOT silently inherited.

footgunFraming: Law-3 NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun. The single-recipient hook design is intentional; the undocumented interaction with a two-staker migration is not. The in-repo orchestrator tests never wire a real (or recipient-guarded) hook to the target, so the ordering constraint is UNTESTED and UNDOCUMENTED.
